summary: We developed an easy-to-use and accessible method of running diagnostic tests and medical examinations to ensure that astronauts are consistently able to examine themselves and make sure of their own mental and physical well-being. Along with this, our project is capable of doing fast-paced emergency diagnostics that can identify and assist users in finding and solving immediate issues in their environment or with crew members. Overall, our project provides users with a simple experience that quickly and efficiently provides them information about their present circumstances, both physically and mentally, stores diagnostic data, and transfers information between space and Earth to get assistance to our users as quickly as possible.
details: Our project aims to provide an easy to understand and accessible method of checking astronauts’ vitals in a visually appealing format. It holds a multitude of benefits for the user, including quick and simple access to emergency diagnostic data and analysis for understanding issues and how to treat them. This project intends to successfully make it a less boring and much more intuitive task to track your vitals while in space and treat issues effectively as they come without struggling with the difficulty of interpreting and traveling through catalogues of medical terminology. In order to complete this project, we used Java, CSS, and TypeScript. We also used Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini to expedite our coding process and improve upon our original code. In order to produce our project, we used a laptop and a PC, as well as GitHub to collaborate on the project. We believe that our project takes creative liberties in how it handles providing information to the user and how it motivates the user to do the various required diagnostic tests, due to our intent in “gameifying” the diagnostic process. Our team focused on the primary factors of ease of access and ease of understanding to maximize the efficiency of the user’s diagnostics and ensuring that all data used in our research was accurate and concise.
